mailq.title: Mail queue
mailq.desc: Outbound deliveries awaiting relay. A pending entry has not been attempted yet; a deferred one failed transiently and retries at the shown time. Flush a deferred entry to retry it now, or delete one to drop it (no bounce is sent).
mailq.confirmDelete: Delete this queued delivery to {0}? No bounce is sent.
mailq.unread: Could not read the mail queue.

taskq.title: Task queue
taskq.desc: Long-running admin operations, such as a directory sync, run here in the background. The table refreshes every five seconds.

avQuarantine.title: Quarantine
avQuarantine.desc: Messages held because antivirus matched a signature. They were not delivered; the recipient and the domain and organization administrators were notified. A system administrator sees every held message, a domain administrator only their domains'.
avQuarantine.none: No messages are held in quarantine.

spamHistory.title: Spam History
spamHistory.desc: The most recent inbound messages scored at delivery. A message over the threshold was filed to the recipient's Junk folder. Reasons list the signals that fired.
spamHistory.retentionDesc: How many scored verdicts this page keeps.
spamHistory.retentionAfter: scored verdicts are kept; older rows are pruned automatically as new mail is scored, so the history never grows unbounded.
spamHistory.retentionInvalid: Retention must be at least 1; setting not saved.
spamHistory.retentionFailed: Could not save the retention setting.
spamHistory.retentionSaved: Retention saved, the MTA applies it within a minute, no restart.

senderAccess.title: Sender allow/block
senderAccess.desc: Rules that override spam scoring at delivery. Changes apply within about a minute, no restart.
senderAccess.rulesDesc: An allowlisted sender skips score-based junking (a forged sender that hard-fails DMARC under an enforcing policy is still junked); a blocklisted sender is always filed to Junk. A pattern is an address or a bare domain, and an exact address beats a domain.
senderAccess.patternRequired: A pattern (email address or domain) is required.

reports.title: Reports
reports.desc: Reports other mail servers send to a hosted domain's postmaster address: DMARC aggregate reports, TLS reports (RFC 8460) and DMARC failure reports. A report is stored only for the domain it was addressed to. A system administrator sees every domain's reports, a domain administrator only their domains'.
reports.warnListBefore: postmaster@{0} is a distribution list. The list delivers a report to its members, so
reports.warnListAfter: . Point postmaster@{0} at a mailbox with an alias instead.
reports.warnMissingBefore: postmaster@{0} does not resolve to a mailbox, so a report sent to it is refused and
reports.failuresDesc: One report per message that failed DMARC at the receiver. Open one to see the failed message's headers.
reports.noFailures: No failure reports in this period.
reports.summaryDesc: Every report in the period, added up.
reports.noTLS: No TLS reports in this period.
reports.noDMARC: No DMARC aggregate reports in this period.
reports.listDesc: Each report as it arrived. Open one to see its records.
reports.retentionDesc: How long stored reports are kept.
reports.sendingDesc: Report back to the domains that ask for DMARC aggregate reports.
reports.retentionHint: Reports are deleted once they are older than their retention window, counted from the time they arrived. 0 keeps them forever. A failure report carries the failed message's headers, which are personal data, so keep it for a shorter time.
reports.aggregateDays: DMARC aggregate and TLS reports, days
reports.sendingHint: When this is on, the server counts the mail it receives from each domain that asks for DMARC aggregate reports, and once a day sends that domain a report to the mailto: addresses its DMARC record names. A report lists the addresses that sent mail claiming the domain, and how each one authenticated. It is sent from noreply at the server's hostname, and it is DKIM-signed only when that hostname has a DKIM key.
reports.postmasterUnread: Could not check the postmaster addresses.
reports.badDomain: The domain filter is not valid.
reports.badStart: The start date is not valid.
reports.badEnd: The end date is not valid.
reports.retentionFailed: Could not save the retention setting.
reports.retentionSaved: Report retention saved; the sweep deletes expired reports within a minute, no restart.
reports.sendingFailed: Could not save the DMARC sending setting.
reports.sendingSaved: DMARC report sending saved; the mail server applies it within a minute, no restart.

reportDetail.reportDesc: The report is the reporter's claim. How it arrived and the DKIM result below are what this server saw. A valid signature proves which domain sent the report, not that its numbers are true.
reportDetail.failureReportDesc: The report is the reporter's claim. How it arrived and the DKIM result below are what this server saw. A valid signature proves which domain sent the report, not that its contents are true.
reportDetail.recordsDesc: One row per source address and result the reporter saw.
reportDetail.headersDesc: Only the failed message's headers are stored, never its body.
reportDetail.dkimNA: not applicable, HTTPS carries no signature

mobileDevices.title: Mobile devices
mobileDevices.desc: Live ActiveSync sessions across all users. The list refreshes every 2 seconds.
mobileDevices.liveDesc: Each device's latest ActiveSync command and when it last reached the server.

syncPolicy.title: Sync policy
syncPolicy.desc: The baseline ActiveSync policy every device receives before a domain or per-user override is merged on top.
syncPolicy.cardDesc: Leave a field unset to leave it unenforced. Password rules (length, complex characters, expiration, history, failed-attempt limit) apply only when DevicePasswordEnabled is Yes.

createDefaults.title: Create defaults
createDefaults.desc: Values pre-filled into the new-domain and new-user forms. An administrator can still change any field before creating.
createDefaults.domainsDesc: Seeds the form that creates a domain.
createDefaults.usersDesc: Seeds the form that creates a user. A domain's own override takes precedence.
